title: Dependencies
headline: The dependency list is lean, and none of this dimension's case rests on what stores use today: 51 runtime packages, none without an importer, and every heavy browser library loads only on the press that needs it. The cost is in when server code loads: the page-view beacon takes about 1.0 s and 177 MB before its first answer where a lean route takes 0.22 s and 64 MB, and with three small import cuts (DP-10, DP-1, DP-3 step 1) its own code, bundled here, loads in 128-144 ms and 50 MB against 549-590 ms and 158 MB today. In the admin, Supabase's client and zod are 39% of the scripts a modern browser loads first on every screen (354 KB of 899 KB), the rich text editor (435 KB) is sent to 21 lists and detail pages, and every admin screen loads the AI manager's whole server side through two action files, a second door that the storefront review's cut does not close. Every P0 fix is a few lines in a few files, moves no data, and is cheapest now, before opening.

clean: No dead dependency: every package in package.json has an importer in src, scripts, e2e or a config file. three and @tiptap/pm have no import of their own but are required peers of @google/model-viewer and tiptap; model-viewer's module build (lib/model-viewer.js) imports the installed three, so three is not bundled twice.

Heavy browser libraries are behind import() at the point of use: @google/model-viewer with three (product-gallery.tsx:349), mediabunny (video-compress.ts:25, :51; animation-make.ts:36), @jsquash/avif (avif-encode.ts:13), the six @codemirror packages (css-panel.tsx:22), the four @stripe browser packages, web-vitals (speed-beacon.tsx:53) and motion (only scroll(), a fallback for browsers without CSS scroll timelines, motion-runtime.ts:258). Each is in 0 route manifests.
Shoppers get no third-party run-time library in their first scripts, held by two checks: src/lib/storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts and e2e/performance.spec.ts.

Tree-shaking works where it matters: no unused simple-icons icon is in any client or server chunk, zod's locales are in no chunk, zod is in exactly one client chunk (the admin's), and postgres.js and PGlite are in no server chunk.
lucide-react is imported by name in 24 files, never as a namespace.

Server-side single-purpose packages are loaded on demand, so their cost follows use: playwright-core and @sparticuz/chromium (browser.ts:11, :15; in 12 route traces only), mammoth and unpdf (knowledge.ts:70, :75; bill-reading.ts:54), subset-font and fontverter (font-trim.ts, the five-minute dispatcher only, 21-25 ms each), web-push (push.ts, reached by 7 routes). A store that does not use these features pays nothing per request. That no store has used them yet is not evidence of anything before opening and is not argued here.
drizzle-orm is used as a sql tag plus drizzle-kit's migration differ. That is a sound use; only the schema's presence at run time is waste (DP-1).

Two Postgres drivers have a recorded reason (client.ts:56-63, D37): pg is the run-time driver; postgres.js serves the build's host read (store-hosts-build.ts), the migration scripts and tests, and is in no function's chunks or trace.
pnpm-workspace.yaml: five overrides, each with its advisory and reason; one patch to Next (D423). CI runs pnpm audit --prod (ci.yml:75).
No package is installed in two versions that both reach run-time code: the 19 names with two or three versions are build and lint tools, plus patch-level copies of pg-protocol and nanoid.

One engine per job: @dnd-kit is the only drag library (8 admin files; native drag events appear in 4 files with at most 2 handlers each); QR codes exist once (lib/qr.ts, one page); Stripe webhook signatures use the SDK's constructEvent. No hand-rolled copy of an installed package was found.

Row checks with zod (typedRows) were measured because 746 of 1,314 calls build their schema inside the call: 14-72 microseconds per read, almost all in back-office modules. Not worth a step; hoisting them would move the cost to import time, which is the scarcer thing.

On Vercel, Next does not preload every route at start (next-server.js:468: only outside minimal mode), so a route's modules load on its first request in an instance, as the measurements assume. Routes that share a function also share loaded modules, so which request pays depends on Vercel's grouping, which was not measured.

findings.title: Every route that reads a store builds the whole page model: 468 schemas for a theme's few fields
findings.evidence: src/lib/page-content.ts is 4,319 lines with 468 zod constructor calls, imported by 251 non-test files. The store reader (server/stores.ts, behind getStore()) reaches it four ways: stores.ts:25 parses the theme, and theme.ts:9 takes two numbers (CONTENT_MAX_MIN, CONTENT_MAX_MAX) from it; theme-elements.ts takes themeElementSchema (page-content.ts:2925, built from the spacing, border, shadow and background schemas) and mapChildBlocks; stores.ts:14 takes the type guard isPageRole from page-roles.ts, whose first line imports newPageContent; and the beacon's visit-record.ts:8 takes two lists of reserved slugs. Cutting the three small imports alone does not free it (walked: theme-elements.ts still reaches it). Measured as bundles in a fresh process: the page model and its 52 files 63-64 ms, 8.2 MB heap, 36 MB RSS (zod alone 18-19 ms, 2.2 MB, 9 MB); the store reader with schema.ts and the Stripe SDK stubbed 127-136 ms, 15.6 MB, 49 MB, against 67-87 ms, 7.5 MB, 29 MB for the health route without the schema. So once DP-10 and DP-1 are done, about half of what the beacon still loads is the page model.
findings.cost: About 45 ms, 6 MB of heap and 20-26 MB of resident memory per cold start (this sandbox) on every route that reads a store but draws no page: the beacons, the tile and cart APIs, webhooks, cron routes. Page routes need the model anyway and gain nothing.
findings.who_pays: The server per new function instance on API and beacon routes. Small beside the hub today; it becomes the largest single piece of the beacon after the other cuts.
fix_steps: Do this as part of code review step 3.2, which already turns src/lib/page-content.ts into a folder with the same exports. Add one constraint to that step: the part-style schemas (spacing, border, radius, shadow, background, size overrides, typography groups) and themeElementSchema live in a leaf file of the folder that imports no block schema, for example src/lib/page-content/part-styles.ts.

src/lib/theme-elements.ts and src/lib/theme.ts import from that leaf file, not from the folder's index; CONTENT_MAX_MIN and CONTENT_MAX_MAX move to a constants file both import; mapChildBlocks moves to a file of plain block helpers without schemas.
Move PAGE_ROLES and isPageRole (page-roles.ts:16-19) to src/lib/page-role-names.ts; page-roles.ts re-exports them; src/server/stores.ts:14 imports from the new file.
Move RESERVED_STORE_PAGE_SLUGS and RESERVED_ARTICLE_SLUGS (page-content.ts:2644-2670) to src/lib/reserved-slugs.ts; page-content re-exports them; src/lib/visit-record.ts:8 imports from the new file.
Add to DP-6's graph test: src/server/stores.ts and the four /api/visit routes may not reach the block schemas' file.
Re-time the beacon after the build (fresh-process load of .next/server/app/api/visit/route.js).
tests_and_rules: Code review step 3.2's own done-when (no importer of @/lib/page-content changed; every block type has its editor, icon, renderer and message): the re-exports keep it true for the 251 importers; only the four files named here change their import path on purpose
src/lib/page-content.test.ts, theme-elements.test.ts, page-roles.test.ts and visit-record.test.ts: must pass unchanged
The database check pages_store_slug_not_reserved is kept in step with RESERVED_STORE_PAGE_SLUGS (comment at page-content.ts:2638): the list only moves file
src/lib/storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts forbids lib/page-content in visitors' scripts: add the new block-schema file to its FORBIDDEN list
docs/audits/code-review-2026-11.md step 3.2 and findings FB6, FB9: note the leaf-file constraint there
depends_on: Code review step 3.2 (One definition per block: page-content.ts becomes a folder), Open
DP-10 and DP-1 (until they land this is a small share of the beacon's load)
findings.done_when: The graph test shows src/server/stores.ts reaching no file that defines a block schema, and a fresh-process load of the built /api/visit route is within 60 ms of /api/health's (today about 800 ms apart).
findings.saving: Estimate from the bundles: up to 45 ms, 6 MB heap and 20-26 MB RSS per cold start on routes that read a store and draw no page. The share of the 468 schemas the theme truly needs was not counted, so the real figure is somewhat lower.
findings.risk: Medium for a small gain if done alone: 251 files import the page model, and a careless split changes import order or creates a cycle. Low when done inside step 3.2 with re-exports. A cycle shows as an undefined schema at import in pnpm test.
findings.already_tracked: Partly: code review step 3.2 (FB6, FB9), Open, splits page-content.ts into a folder but with the same exports and no rule about which file may import which, so by itself it saves nothing at load.
findings.notes: Added by the planner. Worth doing when step 3.2 is done, not before: alone it is a refactor of a 4,319-line module for 45 ms. Recorded now so that step 3.2 is cut along the line that pays.

findings.title: Three Chromium routes are woken every minute whether or not there is work
findings.evidence: pg_cron calls /api/cron/cookie-scan, /api/cron/page-looks and /api/cron/theme-shots every minute (migration lines 96, 101, 103). Each route's trace is 125.4 MB (Chromium 66.8, playwright-core 11.1, sharp 18.8, taxonomy 12.7, chunks 14.0). Chromium itself is started only when there is work (browser.ts uses import()), which is well done. Because the routes are called every minute they stay warm, so the 125 MB is paid at each deploy's cold start, not per call. The cookie-scan call runs two updates and a read of cookie_scans every time (cookie-scans.ts:72-86). Before opening the queues are empty by nature; that shows what an idle wake costs, not that the features are unwanted.
findings.cost: 4,320 function calls a day, each with a net.http_post, a cron_jobs upsert and, for the cookie scan, three statements. Fixed: it does not grow with stores. Small in money.
findings.who_pays: The server (invocations) and the database (writes and scans each minute). Once stores exist more wakes will find work: a weekly scan per store fills about 10% of the cookie scan's minutes at 1,000 stores (estimate).
fix_steps: Do not change this alone: it is one of the nine every-minute routes of the scheduling review's CR-1. Make the scheduler change once, there.

For the cookie scan, a SQL function (a custom migration: pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name cookie_scan_due, then node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs) that returns true when claimScan() would find work: a queued row, a row running for more than ten minutes, or an open site whose last finished scan is a week old (a failed one an hour old). It must mirror claimScan() (src/server/cookie-scans.ts:72 onward) exactly, or claimScan()'s three reads move into it. The pg_cron job posts to the route only when it returns true. A new migration reschedules the job; the baseline is never edited.
For page-looks and theme-shots the same, from the due rule of runPageLooks() (src/server/page-looks.ts) and runThemeShots() (src/server/theme-shots.ts).

Cron health: a one-minute job counts as late after eleven minutes without a finished run (src/lib/cron-health.ts:26-28). Either the SQL check writes a heartbeat to commerce.cron_jobs when it finds nothing, or the three routes are registered with a longer interval in trackedRoute(). Update src/lib/cron-health.test.ts and src/server/cron-runs.int.test.ts with it.
Add a test to src/db/commerce.test.ts for each due function (the rule for any new SQL rule).
tests_and_rules: src/server/cron-routes.scan.test.ts (every cron route has a maxDuration and runs inside trackedRoute): the routes keep both
src/lib/cron-health.test.ts, src/server/cron-runs.int.test.ts: the late rule changes with the heartbeat
src/db/commerce.test.ts: a test per new SQL function; src/db/migration-safety.scan.test.ts must pass
docs/ci-migrations.md and CLAUDE.md 'Database': a new migration through CI, recorded in docs/decisions.md (Migration versions); advisors checked after the deploy
The platform home and Usage and limits read commerce.cron_jobs: they must not show the three routes as late
depends_on: CR-1 of the scheduling review (the nine every-minute routes): this is done there
findings.done_when: With empty queues, commerce.cron_jobs shows no new run of route.cookie-scan, route.page-looks or route.theme-shots over an hour (today 60 each), and the platform home shows none of them late.
findings.saving: Estimate: most of 4,320 calls a day while queues are mostly empty, falling as stores arrive. No cold-start saving.
findings.risk: Low to medium: a queued job starts up to one tick later; a wrong condition leaves a scan waiting, which the cookie page would show as an old scan date; the platform home shows the routes as late unless cron health changes with it.
findings.already_tracked: no in the existing plans; it is a part of this review's scheduling finding CR-1, which should own it.
findings.notes: Kept in this dimension only because Chromium's 125 MB trace is a dependency fact. Read under the owner's clarification: a fixed idle cost of scheduling, not an argument against the three features. The saving shrinks as stores arrive, so it is P2.

findings.title: A 26 MB icon package is installed and parsed each build for 26 paths
findings.evidence: brand-icon.tsx imports 26 named icons from simple-icons, which holds 3,467 (re-counted). The 26 paths total 19,982 bytes. The package is 26 MB installed and its entry module, which the bundler reads on every build to pick those 26, is 5,255,349 bytes. LinkedIn's mark is already hand-kept in the same file because the package dropped it (line 35), and the dependency is one of four with a caret range. Tree-shaking works: no unused icon is in any chunk. The licence is CC0-1.0.
findings.cost: 26 MB of install, a 5.25 MB module parsed per build, and a package that removes brands in major versions. Nothing at run time.
findings.who_pays: The build and CI installs; nobody's browser or function.
fix_steps: Create src/components/brand-marks-data.ts with one entry per network: { path, hex } copied from simple-icons 16.36.0 for the 26 names imported at brand-icon.tsx:1-28, plus the LinkedIn entry now at lines 35-36 and 78. A node one-liner over require('simple-icons') writes the file; say in its header where the paths came from, the version and that the licence is CC0-1.0.
src/components/brand-icon.tsx: delete the simple-icons import and the Object.fromEntries block (lines 46-77); BRANDS becomes the imported data. brandColor() and BrandIcon stay as they are.
package.json: remove simple-icons; run pnpm install so pnpm-lock.yaml follows.
Add a unit test beside src/lib/social-links.test.ts: every SocialNetwork has either a brand mark or a stroked mark, and every path starts with M.
tests_and_rules: src/lib/social-links.test.ts: must pass; gains the coverage test
docs/decisions.md D91 (social media buttons): no rule names the package; no edit
DP-6's dependencies scan would have flagged nothing here (the package is imported); this is a size call, not a dead dependency
findings.done_when: rg -n 'simple-icons' package.json src prints nothing, and du -sm node_modules/.pnpm falls by about 26 MB.
findings.saving: 26 MB less to install; one 5.25 MB parse less per build. The time saved is small and not measured: tidiness, not speed.
findings.risk: Low. A brand that redraws its mark must be updated by hand, as LinkedIn's already is. The footer's social links would show a wrong or empty mark; the unit test catches an empty one.
findings.notes: Costs the build only, so it waits until brand-icon.tsx or the social links are next touched.

findings.title: The Stripe and Supabase SDKs are evaluated by 97% of routes; reading a store imports the Stripe SDK to see if two keys exist
findings.evidence: getStore() computes paymentsOn with platformModes() (stores.ts:300), which calls platformStripe(mode) and so builds, once per instance, a Stripe client just to learn whether two environment keys are set. stores.ts therefore imports stripe.ts, whose first line imports the SDK; stores.ts reaches only 130 source files, so on a lean route this one edge is what brings the SDK (walked: with it cut, /api/visit after DP-10 reaches no Stripe code). In the build the Stripe SDK module (212 KB) is in the chunks of 804 of 830 routes and supabase-js (206 KB) in 803. New measurement: the beacon's own code after DP-10 and DP-1, bundled, loads in 130-143 ms and +18.3 MB heap with the Stripe SDK and in 128-144 ms and +17.1 MB without. The difference is inside the noise. New fact for the fix: 153 test files mock ./stripe and 113 of them supply platformModes: () => ['test'] so that getStore() reports payments on.
findings.cost: As the build holds them, Stripe evaluates in 18-28 ms and supabase-js in about 14 ms (skeptic); on a lean route the planner measured no difference beyond 1 MB of heap. 418 KB of JS compiled in 97% of routes.
findings.who_pays: The server once per new function instance. Small beside the hub itself.
fix_steps: Not now. Take step 1 only when src/server/stores.ts or stripe.ts is next changed for another reason.

Step 1: a new src/server/stripe-keys.ts (server-only, no SDK import) holding platformSecretKey(mode), platformPublishableKey(mode) and platformModes(), built on platformKey() from src/lib/stripe-account.ts. stripe.ts imports and re-exports them, so its 43 importers keep working. stores.ts:182, orders.ts:23 and settings.ts:16 import platformModes from ./stripe-keys.

With step 1, the 113 integration tests that mock ./stripe with platformModes no longer reach getStore() through that mock. Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_TEST and STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_TEST to dummy sk_test_ and pk_test_ values once, in vitest.integration.config.mts (the test.env option, so every worker sees them), so paymentsOn stays true where the tests expect it; run pnpm test:int and fix what still differs.

Step 2 (async stripeFor() and platformStripe(), a lazy storage client in media.ts): only if a measurement on the built routes after DP-1, DP-10 and the hub cuts still shows the two SDKs. 65 call sites would gain an await.
tests_and_rules: 153 test files mock ./stripe; 113 supply platformModes (rg -l 'platformModes: \(\) =>' src -g '*.test.*'): the reason step 1 is not the one-line change it looks
src/server/checkout.int.test.ts:253 sets STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_TEST itself: must keep passing
CLAUDE.md: payment credentials are store settings, never environment variables (D15); the platform's own keys are the exception stripe.ts already reads from the environment: no rule changes
Code review step 4.2 (all environment reads through env.ts, Open): the new file is one more reader to list there
DP-6's graph test would then forbid src/server/stripe.ts on the beacon routes
depends_on: DP-10 and DP-1 first (until then other chains bring the SDK anyway)
findings.done_when: The graph test shows the four /api/visit routes reaching no file that imports the stripe package, and pnpm test:int passes.
findings.saving: Measured: nothing visible in load time on the lean route and about 1 MB of heap; 220 KB less in its bundle. The skeptic's bundled timing gives up to 18-28 ms for Stripe and 14 ms for supabase-js on routes that do not use them.
findings.risk: Step 1: low in the app, medium in the tests (113 mocks change meaning; a test that expected payments on would fail loudly). Step 2: medium, it touches every payment call. Before opening is the cheapest time to touch payment code, but the gain does not justify it.
findings.notes: True but not worth doing now. The planner's measurement puts the gain on a lean route inside the noise, and the test suite's mocks make step 1 an M, not an S. It stays on the list because the edge is a real oddity (a store read builds a payment client to count two keys) and the fix is known when the file is next opened.
